subject.title: feat(imessage): native poll controls for approval prompts

question: After imsg v0.13.4 is released, does its published binary provide the authoritative sender and immutable option-ID contract required to enable native approval polls by default on capable iMessage installations?
rationale: The proposed security boundary crosses into a separately released bridge; source-level fallback handling cannot establish the exact behavior of the distributed bridge binary that production users will run.

options.title: Verify then enable
options.body: Run released-binary iMessage proof that validates sender provenance, option IDs, deny resolution, and fallback behavior on the rebased PR head before marking the PR ready.

options.title: Keep polls experimental
options.body: Retain the code but require an explicit opt-in until the bridge contract is independently documented and verified.

options.title: Defer native polls
options.body: Close or pause the feature if the released bridge cannot provide the required authorization facts without weakening the existing approval boundary.

recommendation.title: Verify then enable
recommendation.body: Run released-binary iMessage proof that validates sender provenance, option IDs, deny resolution, and fallback behavior on the rebased PR head before marking the PR ready.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged iMessage-adjacent authorization work is the strongest current-main provenance for evaluating whether the new ingress shortcut preserves the established trust boundary.
